A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CiteBART study. Their main text, equations, tables, and complete appendices, including image-based prompt examples, are readable and can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original CiteBART benchmark results, ablations, hallucination measurements, cross-dataset examples, and Llama-2 prompting trials.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds benchmark comparisons and exploratory LLM prompting findings.

M1.justification: The architecture, citation masking, Base/Global inputs, and decoding settings remain unchanged. However, v2 Table 1 labels citation-only targets for both pretraining and evaluation, whereas v3 restricts that table to evaluation and adds Figure 1 showing full-context reconstruction during pretraining. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects the documentation or changes the training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use ACL-200, PeerRead, Refseer, and Arxiv for local citation recommendation and retain the same cross-dataset examples. New LLM trials change prompting procedures within this coverage. Multi-citation evaluation is proposed as future work, not performed.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds BM25 and SymTax (SciV) comparisons on all four benchmarks, substantially expanding the primary comparator set beyond BERT-GCN, DualEnh-ws, and HAtten. Those earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: v3 reports HAtten on entire test sets, replacing comparisons explicitly marked as 10k-subset evaluations for Refseer and Arxiv in v2 Table 4. Section 4.6 also introduces prompts using 100 BM25-prefetched candidates for top-10 or single-best selection. CiteBART's stated splits, training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged; EM is relocated, not dropped.

E4.justification: New Section 4.6 adds exploratory analysis of metadata-rich LLM prompting, examining context-length failures, invalid selections, and repetition of the highest-ranked BM25 candidate. The existing ablations, hallucination analyses, cross-dataset cases, and appendix prompt examples are retained.

E5.justification: The hallucination comparison's p < 0.001 statement and ablation significance wording are unchanged. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds BM25 and SymTax results and HAtten MRR values. HAtten R@10 changes from 0.633/0.757/0.454/0.439 to 0.499/0.579/0.339/0.329 across ACL-200/PeerRead/Refseer/Arxiv; these are replacement results under revised reported settings, not established same-setting declines. CiteBART scores, including EM relocated to Table 11, and Tables 5–9 remain unchanged. Section 4.6 adds qualitative LLM failure findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the hallucination-category definitions, and the reasoning equating MaHR and MiHR for fixed-length prediction lists are retained. No mathematical propositions, proofs, or formal derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and main conclusion retain the same claims about end-to-end citation masking, benchmark superiority except on PeerRead, cross-dataset generalization, and hallucination analysis. Additional comparisons support these retained claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and failure discussions. Its new Limitations section addresses assumed citation worthiness, dependence on the training citation pool, unsupported multi-citation contexts and their data requirements, and possible bias toward citing-paper information. Section 4.6 adds interpretations concerning LLM context capacity, ranking reliability, and efficiency.

D1.justification: Figure 1 adds explicit documentation of training versus inference outputs, and Section 4.6 describes candidate metadata and requested LLM outputs. v2's explicit HAtten 2k-prefetch specification is no longer provided. Existing hyperparameters, token limits, hardware, timings, and resource links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Goyal et al. (2024) for SymTax, Robertson and Zaragoza (2009) for BM25, and Jiang et al. (2025) for LLM-based citation recommendation. These receive focused discussion, while the broader literature survey and end-to-end versus retrieval-pipeline positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.6, a Limitations section, and an Exact Match appendix, renumbering the existing LLM appendix from C to D. It also makes localized wording, heading, and acknowledgment edits and adds a repetitive introductory paragraph. Most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds workflow Figure 1 and restructures Table 4 with extra comparator rows and fewer metric columns. The unchanged EM values appear separately in new Table 11. Captions and table placement are adjusted; the original appendix prompt figures are retained unchanged as Figures 2–3.

improvement.justification: The broader comparison in Table 4 and explicit applicability limitations improve the paper's empirical context and qualification of its claims. The gain is limited: CiteBART's results and principal analyses are unchanged, the new LLM trials lack model and sample-count details, and the training-target documentation leaves the procedural ambiguity identified under M1 unresolved.
